introduction: These hundred readings say that every person was created for the betterment of the world: to look beyond private concerns, to treat service as worship, to heal, to educate, to hold office only in order to serve, and to give up comfort and even life for the common good. The passages set beside them show how widely that call has been heard, in the Samaritan of the parable, the Qur’an's steep ascent, Mencius before a king, Marley's ghost and George Eliot's unhistoric acts. Others press hard questions about it: Dostoevsky on loving humanity and not the person nearby, Blake and Wilde on charity that leaves poverty in place, Kipling's burden, Mencius's farmer tugging at his corn, and Martha told that one thing is needful. They are there so that the wish to serve can be examined as well as encouraged.
questions: The readings say service is prayer. What work of yours, paid or unpaid, could be done in that spirit, and what would change if it were?
Dostoevsky's character loves humanity and cannot bear people. How do you keep a concern for the whole world tied to the person in front of you?
Blake and Wilde suspect charity of keeping in place the conditions that make it necessary. What would it mean to serve in a way that also strikes at the root, as Thoreau puts it?
Kipling called the rule of other peoples a service to them. What safeguards keep those who wish to advance the world from deciding for others what their good is?
Several readings ask for sacrifice of comfort, wealth and life; Paul says that without love such sacrifice profits nothing. How can a person tell which is at work in themselves?
Milton concluded that they also serve who only stand and wait. What forms of service are open to someone who can do very little?

outside.why: John Donne wrote that no man is an island, and that any man's death diminishes him because he is involved in mankind.
Jeremiah wrote to the exiles in Babylon: seek the peace of the city, for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.
Thoreau observed that there are a thousand hacking at the branches of evil to one who is striking at the root. How does a person tell a remedy for the age from relief of its symptoms?
James asks his readers to be doers of the word, and not hearers only.
Shakespeare's Portia remarks that if to do were as easy as to know what were good to do, chapels had been churches. What stands between knowing a good and doing it?

A character in Dostoevsky confesses: the more I love humanity in general, the less I love man in particular. How is a universal good intention kept from becoming an excuse to neglect the person nearby?
Tagore tells the worshipper in a dark temple that God is where the tiller is tilling the hard ground and the path-maker is breaking stones.
George Herbert wrote that whoever sweeps a room as for God's laws makes that and the action fine.
The first letter of John says: let us not love in word, neither in tongue, but in deed and in truth.
Wordsworth called the best portion of a good man's life his little, nameless, unremembered acts of kindness and of love.
William Lloyd Garrison took as his motto: our country is the world, our countrymen are mankind.
Paul asks the Philippians to look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
Marley's ghost cries out too late that mankind was his business, and the common welfare was his business.
Mencius asked a king: why must your Majesty use that word profit?
Robert Burns wrote that man's inhumanity to man makes countless thousands mourn.
Micah asks what the Lord requires but to do justly, to love mercy and to walk humbly with thy God.
In the parable a Samaritan bound up a stranger's wounds, set him on his own beast and paid for his care.
Job says of his better days: I was eyes to the blind, and feet was I to the lame, and a father to the poor.
William Blake wrote that pity would be no more if we did not make somebody poor. When does consoling the weak leave untouched what made them weak?
James says that pure religion is to visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction.
Jesus said that they that be whole need not a physician, but they that are sick.
Jesus quotes a proverb he expects to hear: physician, heal thyself. What must be true of those who would be doctors to the world?
Asked to cure a mind diseased, Macbeth's doctor answers that therein the patient must minister to himself. What part of healing can no helper do for another?
Paul writes: bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.
Jesus said that whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones shall not lose his reward.
Paul asks the Romans to be kindly affectioned one to another, distributing to the necessity of others and given to hospitality.
In the parable of the judgment the King says: inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me.
Proverbs says that he that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord.
The first letter of John asks how one who loves not his brother whom he has seen can love God whom he has not seen.
Peter summed up the life of Jesus in a phrase: he went about doing good.
James asks what it profits to say to the hungry, be ye warmed and filled, and give them nothing the body needs.
Jesus told Martha, busy with much serving, that one thing is needful, and that Mary had chosen that good part. When does service itself need to stop and listen?
Leviticus gives the commandment in its oldest form: thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
Asked for one word to serve as a rule for all of life, Confucius answered: reciprocity.
Jesus said: let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works.
Plato said that the beginning is the most important part of any work, especially with a young and tender thing.
The Book of Rites remembers an age when a public and common spirit ruled all under the sky, and people did not love their own parents only.
Jesus likened the kingdom of heaven to leaven which a woman hid in three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.
Kipling in 1899 urged his readers to take up the White Man's burden and serve their captives' need. How is the wish to advance the world kept from becoming a claim to rule those it is advanced for?
Pericles said of the Athenians that their ordinary citizens, though occupied with industry, were still fair judges of public matters.
Isaiah promises one who draws out his soul to the hungry that he shall be like a spring of water whose waters fail not.
Paul recalls words of Jesus: it is more blessed to give than to receive.
Alexander Pope wrote that in faith and hope the world will disagree, but all mankind's concern is charity. If charity is common ground whatever people believe, what do the religions add to it?
The Letter to the Hebrews asks believers to consider one another, to provoke unto love and to good works.
Paul says that though we walk in the flesh, the weapons of our warfare are not carnal.
Isaiah says: learn to do well; seek judgment, relieve the oppressed, judge the fatherless, plead for the widow.
Amos asks that judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream.
Jesus said that the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister.
Ezekiel cries woe to the shepherds of Israel that feed themselves and not the flock.
Madison held that since men are not angels, a government must be obliged to control itself. Can good motives in those who hold office be relied on, or must something else stand beside them?
Plutarch reports that Zeno the Stoic taught that all the inhabitants of the world should regard one another as fellow citizens.
Paul writes: let us not be weary in well doing, for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
Jesus told his followers: ye are the salt of the earth, and asked what use salt is that has lost its savour.
At Gettysburg Lincoln said that it is for the living to be dedicated to the unfinished work.
George Eliot ends her novel by saying that the growing good of the world is partly dependent on unhistoric acts.

Oscar Wilde argued that the proper aim is to reconstruct society so that poverty will be impossible, and that altruistic virtues have hindered it. Does kindness to individuals delay the change that would make it unnecessary?
Jesus said: I must work while it is day; the night cometh, when no man can work.
The Preacher says: whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might.
Confucius said that the determined scholar and the man of virtue will even sacrifice their lives to preserve their virtue complete.
In Plato's Republic justice is said to be doing one's own business, and not being a busybody. Where does forgetting one's own interests for others end and meddling begin?
Jesus said: greater love hath no man than this, that a man lay down his life for his friends.
Paul says that though he give all his goods to feed the poor, and have not love, it profits him nothing. What makes a sacrifice for the world worth something to the world?
The Dhammapada sums up the teaching of the Buddhas: not to commit any sin, to do good, and to purify one's mind.
Jesus washed his disciples' feet and said: ye also ought to wash one another's feet.
Jesus asked what it shall profit a man if he gain the whole world and lose his own soul.
The Qur’an praises those who feed the needy, the orphan and the prisoner, wishing for no reward nor thanks.
The Sayings of the Fathers ask people to be like servants who serve the master without the expectation of receiving a reward.
Socrates told Athens that he was a gadfly given to the state by God, and was condemned for it.
Jesus told his disciples: the servant is not greater than his lord; if they have persecuted me, they will also persecute you.
Marcus Aurelius told himself at dawn: I am rising to the work of a human being.
In the synagogue at Nazareth Jesus read from Isaiah: he hath sent me to heal the brokenhearted, and to set at liberty them that are bruised.
Oliver Goldsmith wrote: ill fares the land, to hastening ills a prey, where wealth accumulates, and men decay.
Macbeth asks the doctor: canst thou not minister to a mind diseased, pluck from the memory a rooted sorrow? What can a spiritual physician offer that medicine cannot?
Jesus said that the tree is known by his fruit, and a good man by the good things he brings forth.
Thoreau called the inventions of his day improved means to an unimproved end. What would it take for the ends to be reformed along with the means?
Walt Whitman saw God's purpose from the first in an earth spanned and connected, the races neighbours, the lands welded together.
The Qur’an says to its Prophet: We sent thee not save as a mercy for the peoples.
Mencius tells of a man of Song who, grieved that his corn was not taller, pulled at it to help it grow. What kinds of zeal for reforming the world injure what they mean to help?
Isaiah hears the promise: I will pour water upon him that is thirsty, and my spirit upon thy seed.
Jesus said that the harvest truly is plenteous, but the labourers are few.
The master in the parable says: well done, thou good and faithful servant.
Jesus said: blessed are the peacemakers, for they shall be called the children of God.
Proverbs says: withhold not good from them to whom it is due, when it is in the power of thine hand to do it.
The Qur’an describes the steep ascent: to free a slave, to feed in the day of hunger an orphan or some poor wretch in misery.
Jesus said that when thou doest alms, thy left hand should not know what thy right hand doeth. How can deeds teach others and still be done in secret?
The Qur’an says that righteousness is not turning the face to East or West, but believing and giving one's wealth to kinsfolk, orphans and the needy.
Theodore Roosevelt gave the credit to the man who is actually in the arena, whose face is marred by dust and sweat and blood.
Paul hopes that his friends at Philippi will shine as lights in the world.
Jesus said: ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good. Is poverty a condition to be relieved in every age, or one that can be ended?
Jesus said to his followers: ye are the light of the world.
Jesus told the seventy to rejoice that their names are written in heaven.
The priests of Israel were given the words: the Lord bless thee, and keep thee, and give thee peace.
The psalm says: behold, how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity.
The Qur’an tells the communities of the world: vie with one another in good works.
The Letter to the Hebrews says: to do good and to communicate forget not.
The Qur’an says in a short early chapter: when thou art relieved, still toil.
Jesus said: seek ye first the kingdom of God, and all these things shall be added unto you.
The psalm says that except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain that build it. What difference does it make to work for human progress with or without turning toward God?
Milton, blind, concluded that they also serve who only stand and wait.
The first letter to Timothy asks for prayers for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life.

matthew-least-of-these.text: For I was an hungred, and ye gave me meat: I was thirsty, and ye gave me drink: I was a stranger, and ye took me in: Naked, and ye clothed me: I was sick, and ye visited me: I was in prison, and ye came unto me. Then shall the righteous answer him, saying, Lord, when saw we thee an hungred, and fed thee? or thirsty, and gave thee drink? When saw we thee a stranger, and took thee in? or naked, and clothed thee? Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came unto thee? And the King shall answer and say unto them, Verily I say unto you, Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me

john-washed-the-disciples-feet.text: If I then, your Lord and Master, have washed your feet; ye also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that ye should do as I have done to you

acts-went-about-doing-good.text: How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him

isaiah-draw-out-thy-soul.text: And if thou draw out thy soul to the hungry, and satisfy the afflicted soul; then shall thy light rise in obscurity, and thy darkness be as the noon day: And the Lord shall guide thee continually, and satisfy thy soul in drought, and make fat thy bones: and thou shalt be like a watered garden, and like a spring of water, whose waters fail not

hebrews-to-do-good-forget-not.text: But to do good and to communicate forget not: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased

romans-not-slothful-in-business.text: Be kindly affectioned one to another with brotherly love; in honour preferring one another; Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord; Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer; Distributing to the necessity of saints; given to hospitality

corinthians-seek-anothers-wealth.text: Let no man seek his own, but every man another's wealth

mark-poor-always-with-you.text: For ye have the poor with you always, and whensoever ye will ye may do them good: but me ye have not always

quran-feed-the-needy.text: And feed with food the needy wretch, the orphan and the prisoner, for love of Him, (Saying): We feed you, for the sake of Allah only. We wish for no reward nor thanks

quran-ascent.text: (It is) to free a slave, And to feed in the day of hunger. An orphan near of kin, Or some poor wretch in misery, And to be of those who believe and exhort one another to perseverance and exhort one another to pity
